summary: Interfaces is strategically coherent but has made zero execution progress since the 2026-03-15 commits. All three reported blockers from yesterday remain open and are aging. The assembly metadata link inconsistency is now 3 days old — a sub-30-minute fix that has not been prioritized. No downstream verification evidence exists. The as-code contract pack (added to PLAN.md on 2026-03-15) has not been started. The product is structurally sound and the priority model is correct, but it risks becoming a permanently deferred backlog item without a deliberate execution scheduling decision.

materialChanges.detail: No commits to products/interfaces/ or assemblies/ since 2026-03-15 (last commit: a33ac35, 'Align as-code rollout in product plans and TDE'). All open blockers have aged by one more day without resolution. No new artifacts, decisions, or evidence added.

topPriorities.title: Resolve Interfaces identity, scope, and ownership boundaries
topPriorities.whyThisMattersNow: Strategic guardrail for all downstream work. Charter is narrowed and documented per D-001; ongoing enforcement is required as cross-cutting boundary issues arise elsewhere in the portfolio.
topPriorities.nextConcreteStep: Keep ownership stance explicit wherever Interfaces is referenced, especially when boundary questions arise in downstream workspaces or other products. No new enforcement needed this cycle.

topPriorities.title: Make the Interfaces assembly real, self-consistent, and consumable — including as-code contract pack
topPriorities.whyThisMattersNow: Assembly has known broken metadata links (now 3 days unresolved). As-code rollout is in PLAN.md but not yet started. Both must be resolved before Priority 3 can close. Blocker is aging.
topPriorities.nextConcreteStep: (a) Correct assembly.yaml broken documentation links — this is a sub-30-minute fix; (b) begin scoping the minimal shared As-Code Contract Pack surface between Lyra OS and PXS.

topPriorities.title: Run one downstream consumption pilot with evidence and one preventive drift guard
topPriorities.whyThisMattersNow: Evidence path is not closed. VERIFY contains unchecked criteria; no linked workflow evidence exists in the product stack. This is the product's core value demonstration and it has not been attempted.
topPriorities.nextConcreteStep: Identify one real workflow, run it against the assembly, record evidence link in VERIFY. Enforce changelog-plus-verification drift guard for meaningful contract changes.

risksOrOpportunities.title: Deferred execution risk — Interfaces becoming a permanently backlogged product
risksOrOpportunities.detail: Interfaces has had zero execution progress for 2 days. All three blockers are aging. Without a scheduling decision or deliberate executor assignment, the product risks drifting into a low-priority maintenance posture that never demonstrates real downstream value. This would undermine its enabling role in the portfolio.
risksOrOpportunities.source: nightly report delta — no git activity since 2026-03-15

risksOrOpportunities.title: Assembly packaging remains not self-consistent — R-002 aging
risksOrOpportunities.detail: The broken assembly links (R-002) have been open 3 days. Each day without a fix makes the assembly less credible as an export surface and erodes confidence in installation/migration mechanics.

risksOrOpportunities.title: Promotion gate remains too thin — R-003 aging
risksOrOpportunities.detail: Without one real downstream workflow with linked verification evidence, the product cannot demonstrate behavioral value or control drift credibly. This is the core maturity gap and has not been attempted.

risksOrOpportunities.detail: The as-code contract pack scope (added 2026-03-15) is a genuine portfolio alignment opportunity. However, if started before the assembly link blocker is fixed and before one downstream verification pass exists, it risks compounding the evidence gap rather than enabling it.
